gen.title: How the three circulation cells link from equator to poles

steps.label: Three circulations shape global flow
steps.quote: Instead of one large circulation in each hemisphere, there are three circulations in each:

steps.label: Warm air rises in Hadley cell
steps.quote: Hadley cell – At low latitudes, air moves toward the equator, where it is heated and rises vertically.

steps.label: Surface air moves poleward in Ferrel cell
steps.quote: Ferrel cell – In this mid-latitude atmospheric circulation cell, air near the surface flows poleward and eastward,

steps.label: Air rises and travels toward the poles
steps.quote: Polar cell – At higher latitudes, air rises and travels toward the poles.

steps.label: Cold air sinks over polar highs
steps.quote: Once over the poles, the air sinks, forming areas of high atmospheric pressure called the polar highs.
